source.author: verg
source.text: Post hos insignem palma per gramina currum victoresque ostentat equos satus Hercule pulchro pulcher Aventinus, clipeoque insigne paternum centum angues cinctamque gerit serpentibus hydram; collis Aventini silva quem Rhea sacerdos furtivum partu sub luminis edidit oras, mixta deo mulier, postquam Laurentia victor Geryone extincto Tirynthius attigit arva Tyrrhenoque boves in flumine lavit Hiberas.
source.text_original: Post hos insignem palma per gramina currum / victoresque ostentat equos satus Hercule pulchro / pulcher Aventinus, clipeoque insigne paternum / centum angues cinctamque gerit serpentibus hydram; / collis Aventini silva quem Rhea sacerdos / furtivum partu sub luminis edidit oras, / mixta deo mulier, postquam Laurentia victor / Geryone extincto Tirynthius attigit arva / Tyrrhenoque boves in flumine lavit Hiberas.
source.text_english: After them, handsome Aventinus, son of handsome Hercules, displays his chariot, brilliant with palm, across the grass and his victorious horses; and he bears on his shield his father’s emblem, the hundred-snaked hydra girded with serpents. This man, a priestess of Rhea, a woman mingled with a god, brought forth in secret at the first light upon the slopes of the Aventine hill, after the Tirynthian victor had reached the Laurentine fields when Geryon was slain and had washed the Iberian cattle in the Tyrrhenian stream.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Protinus Inachiis ultro Tirynthius Argis advolat, Arcadio cuius flammata veneno tela puer facilesque umeris gaudentibus arcus gestat Hylas: velit ille quidem, sed dextera nondum par oneri clavaeque capax.
reuse.text_original: Protinus Inachiis ultro Tirynthius Argis / advolat, Arcadio cuius flammata veneno / tela puer facilesque umeris gaudentibus arcus / gestat Hylas: velit ille quidem, sed dextera nondum / par oneri clavaeque capax.
reuse.text_english: Straightway the Tirynthian flies of his own accord to Argos of Inachus, where Hylas carries for him the poisoned darts and the bows that delight his eager shoulders—Arcadian weapons: he would indeed wish it, but his right hand is not yet equal to the burden, nor able to bear the club.
